question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x + y + 2 z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x + y + 2 z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x + y + 2 z)\,k \\  & =(1)\,i+(1)\,j+(2)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,y=t^{2},$ and $z=t^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(1)\,i+(1)\,j+(2)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,k \\  & =(1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(2 t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((1)\,i+(1)\,j+(2)\,k)\cdot ((1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(2 t)\,k) \\  & =(1)\cdot (1)+(1)\cdot (2 t)+(2)\cdot (2 t) \\  & =(1)+(2 t)+(4 t) \\  & =6 t + 1.\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x z \ln{\left(y \right)})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x z \ln{\left(y \right)})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x z \ln{\left(y \right)})\,k \\  & =(z \ln{\left(y \right)})\,i+(\frac{x z}{y})\,j+(x \ln{\left(y \right)})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\left(t - 2\right)^{2},y=t - 2,$ and $z=\left(t - 2\right)^{3}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(\left(t - 2\right)^{3} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})\,i+(\left(t - 2\right)^{4})\,j+(\left(t - 2\right)^{2} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\left(t - 2\right)^{2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t - 2)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\left(t - 2\right)^{3})\,k \\  & =(2 t - 4)\,i+(1)\,j+(3 \left(t - 2\right)^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((\left(t - 2\right)^{3} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})\,i+(\left(t - 2\right)^{4})\,j+(\left(t - 2\right)^{2} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})\,k)\cdot ((2 t - 4)\,i+(1)\,j+(3 \left(t - 2\right)^{2})\,k) \\  & =(\left(t - 2\right)^{3} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})\cdot (2 t - 4)+(\left(t - 2\right)^{4})\cdot (1)+(\left(t - 2\right)^{2} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})\cdot (3 \left(t - 2\right)^{2}) \\  & =(\left(t - 2\right)^{3} \left(2 t - 4\right) \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)})+(\left(t - 2\right)^{4})+(3 \left(t - 2\right)^{4} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)}) \\  & =5 t^{4} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)} + t^{4} - 40 t^{3} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)} - 8 t^{3} + 120 t^{2} \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)} + 24 t^{2} - 160 t \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)} - 32 t + 80 \ln{\left(t - 2 \right)} + 16.\end{aligned}
$$
